thread:
maria_ops: heads up — we started seeing sustained GPU pool saturation in us-west this morning, queues growing >1200 requests and tail latency spiking for interactive routes. looks like autoscale couldn't catch up after the early-morning traffic burst.
benja: saw that. metrics show 94–97% util on the v100 pool for ~30m. ingress rate still high, backlog growing. any sign of noisy tenants?
maria_ops: not obvious yet. per-route breakdown: chat-high and embeddings-batch are the main drivers. chat-high is pinned to r1 models, many long-context requests.
raj_sre: putting this on the incident channel too, but quick ops question — can we apply an admission-control dialback that rejects or downgrades long-context requests for non-enterprise tiers? we should avoid cross-region spill until we evaluate cost.
sre-oncall: agreed we need a fast mitigation. two options: 1) soft-dialback: reduce concurrency and apply per-request token cap; 2) model-fallback: route to a smaller quantized variant for best-effort traffic. both have tradeoffs on latency and quality.
benja: prototype rule idea (pseudo-config):
```json
{
  "route": "chat-high",
  "when": "gpu_util > 90% && queue_depth > 500",
  "actions": [
    {"type": "deprioritize", "targets": ["free-tier"]},
    {"type": "fallback", "model": "redwood-small-8q"},
    {"type": "tag", "reason": "dialback-183600"}
  ]
}
```
maria_ops: I like fallback+deprioritize. can we also emit a capacity-signal so routing layers know to stop spilling to eu unless explicitly allowed? cross-region spill is expensive and increases p99 due to network.
raj_sre: yes — add a tiebreaker: allow spill only if local queue depth > 2000 OR critical tenant flag. that keeps most traffic local.
sre-oncall: note on cost: preliminary calc — routing 10% of requests to eu-west for an hour adds ~$3.8k egress and infra delta. fallback to small model saves ~45% token-cost but may reduce quality on some prompts. need product buy-in.
benja: quick experiment suggestion: apply fallback to 5% sample of chat-high for 10m and run quality eval on known prompts. should be low risk.
maria_ops: rolling out sample now. infra-bot: started canary rollout job id=rb-183600-c1 :robot_face:
infra-bot: job rb-183600-c1: applied route overrides to 5% of chat-high, fallback=redwood-small-8q, window=10m.
raj_sre: monitoring dashboards — queue depth decreased by ~18% in the canary shards. util down ~6%. promising.
sre-oncall: good. next step: if canary stable, expand to 25% and enable admission token cap for free-tier (max input tokens 1024). also add metric: fallback_rate by tenant and quality_regressions.
benja: question: how do we ensure warm pool behavior for the fallback model? cold starts could negate benefits.
maria_ops: we have a tiny warmpool for redwood-small-8q in us-west but it only has 2 nodes. I'll bump to 6 for the next 30m during rollout.
raj_sre: also adding a transient prefer-local routing policy: prefer_local=true unless prefer_local_disabled or queue_depth_local > 2000. pushing config now.
infra-bot: config apply: prefer_local=true, spill_threshold=2000, fallback_model=redwood-small-8q, admission_token_cap=1024.
sre-oncall: tracked action items: (1) expand canary to 25% if no quality regressions in 10m (owner: benja), (2) increase warmpool for small model (owner: maria_ops), (3) emit capacity-signal on /v1/capacity (owner: raj_sre), (4) cost estimate for cross-region spill (owner: finance-eng, ping @benja).
benja: allocating check on noisy tenants — running quick aggregation to find top 10 tenants by token-hours. will share list in 10m.
maria_ops: if anyone sees p99 dropping but not p50, that's likely queue prioritization kicking in. expect some increased latency for deprioritized requests.
raj_sre: FYI engineers — if you want exceptions for specific customers, add tenant flag "critical_sla": true. will require approval.
benja: can we add a short fallback banner to the API response when a fallback happens? helpful for debugging and customer comms.
sre-oncall: yes — add header X-Redwood-Fallback: redwood-small-8q; users will see the change.
maria_ops: expanding canary to 25% now. infra-bot: job rb-183600-c2 started, scope=25%.
infra-bot: job rb-183600-c2: finished. no quality-regression alerts in the sample window.
raj_sre: metrics update: queue depth -40% in affected shards, pool util down to ~88%. spill to eu-west is still off.
benja: great. follow-up: prepare a postmortem note listing mitigation timeline and a plan to invest in faster warmstart and predictive autoscaling to avoid dialbacks.
maria_ops: agreed. I'll draft the postmortem and link dashboards. thanks all. :thumbsup:
